50 US States in Alphabetical Order (Copy & Paste Lists)

By
Bobby Kania
-
October 29, 2026
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 18:25
Instaread

There are 50 states in the United States. The country also includes Washington, D.C. (a federal district, not a state) and 5 major inhabited territories. Alphabetically, the first state is Alabama and the last is Wyoming. The “lower 48” are the contiguous states, meaning all states except Alaska and Hawaii.

US Territories in Order

The most well-known US territories are as follows:

  • American Samoa
  • Guam
  • Northern Mariana Islands
  • Puerto Rico
  • U.S. Virgin Islands

The US also owns many territories around the world located in the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean. Several of these are unincorporated, unorganized territories which means they are just administrative districts. Here are all of the US territories in alphabetical order:

  • American Samoa
  • Baker Island
  • Guam
  • Howland Island
  • Jarvis Island
  • Johnston Atoll
  • Kingman Reef
  • Midway Atoll
  • Navassa Island
  • Northern Mariana Islands
  • Palmyra Atoll
  • Puerto Rico
  • US Virgin Islands
  • Wake Island

FAQs

Is Washington, D.C. Considered a State?

No, currently Washington, D.C. is not considered a state so we did not include it in the list of 50 states above.

What Are the American Territories?

How Many States Are in the United States?

There are 50 states in the United States. Hawaii was the last state admitted to the Union, on August 21, 1959.

What Are the Lower 48 States?

The lower 48 states are the 48 contiguous states, which means every state except Alaska and Hawaii. See the full list in the Lower 48 States section above.

What Is the Largest and Smallest State?

Alaska is the largest state by area and Rhode Island is the smallest.

Which State Is First and Last Alphabetically?

Alabama is first alphabetically and Wyoming is last.
